target_customer: Website owners who wanted to measure and offset the carbon footprint of their traffic
problem: Sites had no easy way to quantify the emissions of serving visitors. CO2Stats estimated them and bought renewable energy certificates.
business_model: Flat rate service based on cumulative client power use, with a badge
product_category: Carbon footprint analytics and offsets for websites

founders.name: Alexander Wissner-Gross
founders.background_notes: Computer scientist with academic ties to Harvard and MIT per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A tracking widget and a footprint model using power mix data, modest engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Estimation formula and offset purchase were copyable, with no data or network effect.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Nobody large was targeting the wedge. Acquirer in 2016 not identified.

market_need_then: Green web hosting and carbon offsets drew attention in 2008, but no demand metrics were found. BuiltWith shows 487 historical and 16 live sites using the widget.

identity.visual_style: Clean energy badge shown on participating sites

branding.brand_signature: Clean energy badge on partner sites

brand_strength.rationale: A public badge gave visibility and TechCrunch covered the launch in 2008, but evidence of wider recognition is thin.

outcome_analysis: CO2Stats launched its full service in August 2008 after YC S08, but no funding history or traction data was found. Directories say it was acquired in December 2016 without naming the buyer, so the deal terms and reason for the end of the product are not public.
notes: Acquisition date comes from the YC one liner and directories and no acquirer was found. Wikipedia places the company in Cambridge, MA while YC says Boston. The domain co2stats.com now hosts an unrelated looking page carbon checker, so it is not evidence of the original company. The 2008 TechCrunch piece named no competitors, so the list is empty. Founding year not found. Directory status is Inactive while the exit is an acquisition, consistent because the product was absorbed or ended after the December 2016 deal.
